extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, state drinking water regulators, and certified environmental laboratories
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures for monitoring, sampling, analysis, and compliance determination for chemical and radiological contaminants in public drinking water systems under 40 CFR part 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring during designated compliance periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public water system shall monitor at the time designated by the State within each compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must follow the timing specified by the State for each compliance period; repeated in multiple paragraphs (e.g., paragraph (h)(17)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance demonstration for new systems or new sources
rubrics_metrics.description: All new systems or systems that use a new source of water that begin operation after January 22, 2004 must demonstrate compliance with the MCL within a period of time specified by the State and comply with initial sampling frequencies specified by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine and increased monitoring frequencies shall be conducted in accordance with the section requirements; similar provisions exist for other date thresholds (e.g., systems beginning use after other dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location — groundwater systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater systems shall take a minimum of one sample at every entry point to the distribution system which is representative of each well after treatment (sampling point). Each sample must be taken at the same sampling point unless conditions make another sampling point more representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling point = entry point representative of each well after treatment; changing sampling point allowed only if more representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location — surface water systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface water systems shall take a minimum of one sample at points in the distribution system that are representative of each source or at each entry point to the distribution system after treatment (sampling point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface water systems include systems with a combination of surface and ground sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling when multiple sources are combined
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system draws water from more than one source and the sources are combined before distribution, the system must sample at an entry point to the distribution system during periods of normal operating conditions (i.e., when water representative of all sources is being used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sampling occurs when blend is representative of all sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency for organic contaminants (§141.61(c)) — initial and repeat
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community and non-transient non-community water system shall take four consecutive quarterly samples for each contaminant during each compliance period beginning with the initial compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems serving >3,300 persons with no detection in initial period may reduce to two quarterly samples in one year during repeat periods; systems ≤3,300 persons with no detection may reduce to one sample per repeat period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver application for reduced sampling frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community and non-transient water system may apply to the State for a waiver from the requirement of taking four consecutive quarterly samples; a system must reapply for a waiver for each compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is applied per compliance period; approval is at State discretion based on evaluation factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: State factors for granting waivers (organic contaminants)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may grant a waiver after evaluating: knowledge of previous use of the contaminant in the watershed/zone of influence; previous analytical results; proximity to potential point/non-point contamination sources; environmental persistence and transport; protection of water source (well depth, soil type, well casing integrity); elevated nitrate levels; use of PCBs in water-related equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no previous use is found, a waiver may be granted. If previous use is unknown or present, the listed factors shall be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when an organic contaminant is detected
rubrics_metrics.description: If an organic contaminant is detected in any sample, each system must monitor quarterly at each sampling point which resulted in a detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may decrease quarterly monitoring only after determining system is reliably and consistently below the MCL; minimum datasets required before that determination (groundwater: ≥2 quarterly samples; surface water: ≥4 quarterly samples). After determination, State may allow annual monitoring (during quarter that previously yielded highest result). Systems with 3 consecutive annual non-detections may apply for waiver. Detection of certain related contaminants triggers analysis for all related contaminants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring following violation of §141.61(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems which violate the requirements of §141.61(c) must monitor quarterly. After a minimum of four quarterly samples show compliance and the State determines the system is reliably and consistently below the MCL, the system shall monitor at the frequency specified for reduced monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State determination required to reduce frequency after demonstrated compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State confirmation samples and error deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may require a confirmation sample for positive or negative results; if required, the result must be averaged with the first sampling result and the average used for compliance determination. States have discretion to delete results of obvious sampling errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirmation sampling window and averaging required; State may exclude obvious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositing for organic contaminant monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may reduce total number of samples by allowing compositing. Composite samples from a maximum of five sampling points are allowed, provided detection limit of method used is < one-fifth of the MCL. Compositing must be done in the laboratory and analyzed within 14 days of collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composite detects contaminant, follow-up individual sampling within 14 days at each included sampling point; duplicates of original samples may be used instead of resampling if available and analyzed/reported within 14 days; compositing among different systems permitted for systems serving ≤3,300 persons, but for >3,300 persons compositing only within a single system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determination at sampling-point level
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with §141.61(c) shall be determined based on the analytical results obtained at each sampling point. If one sampling point is in violation of an MCL, the system is in violation of the MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems monitoring more than once per year, compliance is by running annual average at each sampling point; other rules apply for annual or less frequent monitoring (see separate criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Running annual average and immediate violation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems monitoring more than once per year, compliance with the MCL is determined by a running annual average at each sampling point. If any sample result will cause the running annual average to exceed the MCL at any sampling point, the system is out of compliance immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If system fails to collect required number of samples, compliance based on total number collected; if a sample result is less than the detection limit, zero is used to calculate annual average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection definition for organics (paragraph (h)(18))
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection is defined as greater than or equal to specified concentrations for each contaminant (table of contaminants with detection limits in mg/L provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific numeric detection limits provided for each listed contaminant (e.g., Alachlor .0002 mg/L; 2,3,7,8-TCDD .000000005 mg/L; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory certification and performance evaluation (PE) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses shall only be conducted by labs certified by EPA or the State which must analyze Performance Evaluation (PE) samples at least once a year by each method for which certification is desired and achieve quantitative results within specified acceptance limits for each contaminant included in the PE sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance limits are provided per contaminant (percent or '2 standard deviations' or specific ranges like '0-200' for PCBs as decachlorobiphenyl); labs failing to meet limits presumably cannot be certified for that method.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCB analysis methods and reanalysis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems monitoring for PCBs shall analyze each sample using Method 508.1, 525.2, 508 or 505. Users of Method 505 may have more difficulty achieving required Aroclor detection limits. If PCBs (as one of seven Aroclors) are detected using Method 505 or 508, the system shall reanalyze the sample using Method 508A to quantitate PCBs (as decachlorobiphenyl). Compliance with the PCB MCL is determined based upon quantitative results using Method 508A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aroclor-specific detection limits table provided; method-specific capabilities and limitations noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical monitoring data to satisfy initial monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: If monitoring data collected after January 1, 1990 are generally consistent with §141.24(h), the State may allow systems to use that data to satisfy the initial compliance period monitoring requirement beginning January 1, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may grandfather historical data for initial monitoring under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority to increase monitoring frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may increase the required monitoring frequency where necessary to detect variations within the system (e.g., seasonal fluctuations, changes in water source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may also require more frequent monitoring or confirmation samples at its discretion (applies in multiple sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority to determine compliance and initiate enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The State has the authority to determine compliance or initiate enforcement action based upon analytical results and other information compiled by their sanctioned representatives and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears repeatedly (e.g., paragraph (h)(16) and radioactivity sections) — State discretion in enforcement and compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioactivity analysis methods and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses for radioactivity contaminants (gross alpha, radium-226, radium-228, uranium, man-made radionuclides, etc.) shall be conducted in accordance with specified EPA/Standard Methods/ASTM/USGS/DOE methods listed in the table, or alternative methods listed in appendix A, or equivalents approved by EPA under §141.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific method citations and references are provided; incorporation by reference details and sources for obtaining methods are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioanalysis detection limit definition (precision-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: For radioactivity monitoring, the detection limit is defined as that concentration which can be counted with a precision of ±100% at the 95% confidence level (1.96σ where σ is the standard deviation of the net counting rate of the sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detection limits for specific radionuclides are given in Table B and Table C (e.g., gross alpha 3 pCi/L; radium-226 1 pCi/L; tritium 1,000 pCi/L; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding and averaging for radioactivity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To judge compliance with the MCLs listed in §141.66, averages of data shall be used and shall be rounded to the same number of significant figures as the MCL for the substance in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow significant-figure rounding conventions consistent with MCL precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial monitoring and grandfathering for radionuclides in CWSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems must conduct initial monitoring for gross alpha, radium-226, radium-228, and uranium (four consecutive quarterly samples if no acceptable historical data) by specified deadlines; States may allow historical data from specified compliance periods (June 2000–Dec 8, 2003) to satisfy initial monitoring under conditions and written State findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may waive final two quarters of initial monitoring if prior two quarters below detection limit; if initial average above MCL, quarterly sampling continues until four consecutive quarters at or below MCL (unless different schedule in formal compliance agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced monitoring schedules for radionuclides
rubrics_metrics.description: States may allow reduced future monitoring frequency (from once every 3 years to once every 6 or 9 years) at each sampling point based on initial monitoring averages relative to detection limits and fractions of the MCL (criteria differ for gross alpha/uranium vs. combined radium-226+228).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if average below detection limit → one sample every nine years; if average ≥detection but ≤1/2 MCL → every six years; if >1/2 MCL but ≤MCL → every three years. Reduced-monitoring results determine subsequent monitoring schedule; exceedance on reduced monitoring triggers quarterly sampling until four consecutive quarters below MCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositing for radionuclide quarterly monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: To fulfill quarterly monitoring requirements for gross alpha, radium-226, radium-228, or uranium, a system may composite up to four consecutive quarterly samples from a single entry point if analysis is done within a year of the first sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical result from the composited sample treated as average for compliance and future monitoring frequency; if composited result >1/2 MCL, State may direct additional quarterly samples before allowing reduced monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross alpha substitution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A gross alpha particle activity measurement may be substituted for radium-226 provided gross alpha ≤5 pCi/L, and for uranium provided gross alpha ≤15 pCi/L. The gross alpha measurement shall have a 95% confidence interval (1.65σ) for radium-226 and uranium. When used in lieu, gross alpha result is used to determine future monitoring frequency; if gross alpha < detection, 1/2 detection limit used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitution permitted only under specified numeric thresholds and confidence interval requirements; substitution affects monitoring frequency decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta particle and photon radioactivity monitoring and screening rules
rubrics_metrics.description: CWSs designated by the State as vulnerable must sample quarterly for beta emitters and annually for tritium and strontium-90 at each entry point; if gross beta minus potassium-40 running annual average ≤50 pCi/L (screening level), State may reduce monitoring to once every 3 years. For systems contaminated by nuclear facility effluents, similar requirements apply with different screening levels (e.g., ≤15 pCi/L) and sampling protocols (monthly composites, iodine-131 daily composites, recommended procedures described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems near nuclear facilities may use nuclear facility surveillance data if State approves applicability; if screening exceeded, analysis to identify major radionuclide constituents and dose calculations are required; exceedance of MCL requires monthly monitoring until rolling average of 3 monthly samples demonstrates compliance.
